simple.meaning: שְׁבַח (shᵉbach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to adulate , i.e. adore.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:23. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׁבַח (H7624).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שְׁבַח (shᵉbach) / H7624 is traced through Daniel 2:23, Daniel 4:31, Daniel 4:34, Daniel 5:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: I thank you, and praise you,

timeline.evidenceText: I thank you, and praise you,
While the word was in the king’s mouth, a voice came from the sky, saying, “O king Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: ‘The kingdom has departed from you.
At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever;
They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of bronze, of iron, of wood, and of stone.

but have lifted up yourself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before you, and you and your lords, your wives, and your concubines, have drunk wine from them. You have praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which don’t see, or hear, or know; and you have not glorified the God in whose hand your breath is, and whose are all your ways.
